verdictOnCurrentFilms: Generic, and in three specific ways that are craft failures, not taste. (1) The blurred, zoomed copy of the same photo behind every plate is the pillarbox-filler trick; it invents a light source that does not exist in the archive, and it turns every exhibit the colour of its own mat (Douglass's orange daguerreotype mat floods the frame mustard; the Persia seal spills amber haze, so a lapis exhibit plays gold). (2) Black levels do not match: the Persia seal sits in a visible black rectangle on a lighter haze, the engraving frame floats on brown, the Ford portrait sits on grey smoke. The seam is the first thing you see. (3) The caption is a rounded translucent box in Times-like serif laid across the bottom of the photograph (it eats the Highland Park chassis, the Seal, the base of the Baltimore engraving) with a 11px credit top-right that no one can read; no exhibit font, ink colour or script appears anywhere, so Douglass, Ford and Persia are one template. Also: 18-second dead holds on a still with no motion, a dip-to-dim crossfade (Douglass frame 3 is a half-faded engraving, which reads as a glitch), no on-screen RECONSTRUCTION label beyond the tiny credit. Honest credit: the photographs themselves are correctly primary and ungraded, the faceless Ford frames (boy at the bench, Quadricycle seen from behind) are right, and Persia's no-face rooms are right. Keep all of that and rebuild everything around it.
concept: The Plate. Every film is built like a compositing job whose rule is that the photograph is the locked plate and everything else is made to live in its light. The archive scan is never graded, filtered, blurred or recoloured; instead the ground, type, rules, maps and shadows are sampled FROM the plate (black point, paper tone, grain structure, light direction) so graphics look like they were in the room when the photograph was taken. Each exhibit then gives that same plate its own physical stage: Ford = the parts bin and stencil bay, Douglass = the composing stick and handbill forme, Persia = the road line over faded script, Partition = a map with one line drawn on it. One system (same grid, same caption position, same timing grid, same honesty marks), four material worlds, and nothing that looks like it was added afterwards. The seam you cannot find is the whole premium feeling.
titleSequence: About 12 s, same four-beat structure in every film, exhibit-specific materials. 0-1.5 s: black with 6 s of room tone (no music). 1.5-6 s: the exhibit's first archive photograph is SET on the ground (Douglass daguerreotype, Highland Park line, Xi'an stele rubbing or seal, Partition refugee-road/ station photograph); it arrives by the exhibit's own lock-up move (see transitions) in 10-14 frames, then holds with a 3% maximum push over the whole hold, 2x-supersampled, no blur backdrop. 6-10 s: the title is built in the exhibit's face and lights from the plate side (a physical slow shadow, not a glow): Ford ANTON caps in #ff4b1f stamped through a stencil mask with 2 frames of 1.5 px registration shake; Douglass Abril Fatface set in four slugs, dates in slab, in #d9b36a with real ink-squash on the edges (displacement map from a scanned handbill); Persia Cormorant Garamond with a real Syriac line and the Stele's own Chinese title large behind at 8 percent, rising to 35 percent for the 2 s of the title and then falling back; Partition in Fraunces, the title in Urdu, Hindi, Punjabi and English at equal cap height in one block with a madder line cutting beneath it left to right. 10-12 s: the key card: three marks (ARCHIVE in plain mono, RECONSTRUCTION in the red-outlined stamp, the credit line) with the single sentence 'Real photographs first. Paintings are labelled.' Held 2 s, cut on the first narration breath. No year counter, no word-by-word reveal, no letterbox bars.
typography: Frame 1920x1080 at 24 fps; type sized for TV. Caption: Source Serif 4 Text 46 px on 62-character measure, max 2 lines, sentence case, off-white #f4efe6 at full contrast on the ground colour, in a reserved bottom band 190 px high so the caption NEVER covers a photograph (photograph max height 700 px, bottom edge fixed at y=770). No box, no pill. Credit line: IBM Plex Mono 22 px, #a79f94, left-aligned directly under the photograph's left edge, full credit, never top-right. RECONSTRUCTION: IBM Plex Mono 700 22 px, tracked 0.14 em, 1.5 px #ff6b57 outline stamp, pinned above the painting's top-left corner for the entire time the painting is on screen (it is the only tracked-caps label in the system, so it alone shouts), plus a one-line evidence note in the credit slot. Titles and lower thirds per exhibit. FORD: Anton 150 px titles, Anton 64 px numerals and place names, caps, tight, #ff4b1f only on type and rules, never as a fill behind a photograph. DOUGLASS: Abril Fatface 170 px titles, Alfa Slab One 56 px for dates and place (handbill slab), #d9b36a; no ligature kerning tricks, set tight like wood type. PERSIA: Cormorant Garamond 500, 110 px titles, italic for dates, #4f7cff only on the route line and dots, text in warm off-white; real Noto Serif Syriac and Noto Serif SC set at 420 px behind at 8 percent, proofed by a native reader before render (credited in end card). PARTITION: Fraunces 130 px (opsz 144, SOFT 0) for English; Urdu in Noto Nastaliq Urdu, Hindi in Noto Serif Devanagari, Punjabi in Noto Serif Gurmukhi, each optically sized to the same x-height as Fraunces, Urdu right-aligned with correct RTL shaping; madder #e8553d on the line and dates only. All type is rendered in the browser with document.fonts.ready awaited and animated per frame from a pure function of time (no CSS transitions), so every frame is reproducible. Numerals are tabular; old-style figures only in Persia.
captionsAndLowerThirds: Captions are the narration's own sentences, one sentence per card, swapped on the sentence boundary with a 6-frame opacity change (the one place a dissolve is allowed); no karaoke word highlighting, no box. A card that would run past 2 lines is split at a clause, never shrunk. Lower thirds are placed in the same band as the caption but only appear on first entrance of a person, place or date, as a 2-line unit: line 1 exhibit display face (name or place), line 2 Plex Mono (role, year, source); it enters 8 frames after the cut and leaves 8 frames before the next. Maximum one lower third per 20 s. Credit line is always on screen under every archive photograph for the whole of its hold, and the evidence note under every reconstruction. Content-gated shots get a 3 s plain card first (white on ground: 'The next section describes violence. Skip with any key.') and never have a lower third. The Persia lines read in Persian/Syriac names are spelled once in Latin and once in the real script in the lower third, no transliteration-only.
transitions: 1. BREATH CUT (default, about 60 percent of all cuts): a hard cut placed 2-3 frames AFTER the last phoneme of a sentence, in the narrator's breath gap, no effect, no sound. Any other transition has to justify itself against this one. 2. LINE STAMP (Ford, between rooms/eras): a 3-frame year numeral slam in Anton (scale 118% to 100%, 2-frame registration shake of 3 px) while a #ff4b1f bar wipes left to right over 8 frames; the photo cut happens underneath on frame 4; paired with a time-clock punch sound; 14 frames total. 3. FORME LOCK (Douglass): four gold rules slide in from the frame edges and lock onto the rectangle of the incoming plate over 10 frames with an ease-out and a 1-frame overshoot; the old plate drops out on frame 5, new plate fades up under the rules over 6 frames; sound is a platen thump on lock. 4. ROAD WIPE (Persia): a lapis hairline already drawn across the frame becomes the seam; the old image exits left and the new enters right along it over 18 frames with a 40 percent counter-parallax on the ghost script behind; ease in-out, no blur. 5. MAP LINE CUT (Partition): a madder line draws left to right across the full frame in 20 frames with hand irregularity (low-frequency noise, 6 px amplitude); the image on one side of the line changes first, the other side 6 frames later, so the line is literally the cut; drawn with a pencil scratch, then silence. 6. SAME-ERA DISSOLVE: a 12-frame cross-dissolve, only between two archive photographs of the same year and place, never between archive and painting, never through black. 7. RECONSTRUCTION GATE (archive to painting): the plate cuts away to the bare exhibit ground for 10 frames, the RECONSTRUCTION stamp and the evidence note are set FIRST, then the painting fades up over 18 frames to full opacity; it exits by a plain cut. 8. SILENCE HOLD (gated or heavy moments, including Ford's printed Dearborn Independent pages and Partition violence cards): no transition effect at all, a 1.5 s hold of the plain still before narration continues, score fades 12 frames earlier, nothing animates over the document.
motionGraphics: Every graphic is vector, built in HTML/SVG/canvas, driven by time, and shadowed from the plate's light direction. FORD: (a) the 12.5 hours to 93 minutes assembly-line chart: two bars on a belt drawn to true scale (750 min vs 93 min), Anton numerals counting over 36 frames with ease-out, bars grow in 18 frames, lands on the stressed word 'ninety-three'; (b) the Five Dollar Day: two stacked wage tokens $2.34 and $5.00 to scale, plus the line 'reported 1914 daily wage' (source credit); (c) Model T count: 150 small chassis squares each = 100,000 cars, filling like a line, 15 million total, 4 s. DOUGLASS: (a) the 1845 title page is used as the graphic itself: slow 8 percent push onto 'WRITTEN BY HIMSELF' on the real scan, then an ink bracket draws around it in 8 frames, nothing retyped over it; (b) a two-line quote only where the source is a primary text, set in the slab with each LINE (not word) lifting 4 px over 10 frames; (c) a printed-handbill date block that locks up with Forme Lock. PERSIA: (a) the route: a schematic lapis line Seleucia-Ctesiphon, Merv, Chang'an drawn at constant speed across about 14 s with dots at 410, 635, 781 as the narration says them, labelled SCHEMATIC ROUTE (no terrain fakery, only named cities); (b) ghost script that slowly drifts at 10 px/s opposite the image move; (c) the stele inscription date 781 resolves from the real Chinese characters, not typed over them. PARTITION: (a) the line: a madder line crosses Punjab and Bengal on a flat soot map over 16 s, with stamps 3 June, 14-15 August, 17 August 1947 at their true points in the film; (b) displacement shown as a RANGE band with explicit ends and the words 'estimates differ', never a single dramatic number; (c) place names appear in the local script first, English second. No stock particles, no lens flares, no glow, no 3D camera moves through photographs.

perExhibit.douglass: Ground #14110d, gold #d9b36a, Abril Fatface with slab dates. Kill the mustard haze and the half-faded engraving. Daguerreotype set on iron with a thin gold rule frame, orange mat left exactly as scanned, a contact shadow cast down and right. Forme Lock for every era change; the 1845 title page is zoomed and bracketed, never decorated; the Baltimore engraving and the young-man silhouettes carry the early rooms, no invented face. Gold appears only on rules and type, never as a wash. Slow handbill-paper grain is sampled from the 1845 scan and lives only on type and ground.
perExhibit.ford: Ground #1a1411, signal red-orange #ff4b1f, Anton caps, stencil and parts-bin feel via type, rules and numerals, not textures pasted over photos. Keep the two back-turned reconstructions, each with the stamp set first; the real Hartsook portrait and the Highland Park line photo stay big and uncovered. Line Stamp between eras, the three line-speed charts, a time-clock tick as the only recurring sound. The Beliefs and Morals section uses the SAME type and caption grammar, Breath Cut and Silence Hold only, no red-orange stamp, the printed Dearborn Independent pages shown whole and readable for at least 4 s each and never animated over; the pride is documented, the hard truth is not staged.
perExhibit.persia: Ground #0c1020, lapis #4f7cff, Cormorant Garamond, real Syriac and Chinese stele script large and faded behind. Remove all amber. Match the ground's black point to the seal photo's actual black so its rectangle vanishes (match the graphics to the plate, never grade the plate). Road Wipe throughout; the route graphic carries the structure; every reconstruction is places and objects only. Every line of script is proofed by a native reader and credited.
perExhibit.partition: Ground #120f0c soot, madder #e8553d, Fraunces; the title in Urdu, Hindi, Punjabi and English at equal weight. The map line is the one big gesture of the film, drawn across the frame in real time with a sparing pencil sound; Map Line Cut for era changes; a 3 s content card before any violence and the gated photographs left out of the default cut. Silence Hold on the hardest passages; displacement figures as ranges; schematic map labelled as such.

soundTies: All timing comes from forced-alignment word timestamps on the finished narration (the same transcription pipeline already used for lyric sync), not from eyeballing. Cuts and swaps land 2-3 frames after the last phoneme of the sentence; numerals and route dots land on the stressed word of the sentence that says them (the number fires 3 frames before the vowel peak so the eye and ear arrive together); stamps, locks and line draws trigger a physical sound at the frame of impact (time-clock tick, platen thump, pencil scratch, a plain low drone swell for Road Wipe, never exotic sample clichés), at -18 LUFS relative to narration, and everything ducks 14 dB under speech with a 12-frame attack. Score is a single bed per film that ends 12 frames before any Silence Hold; narration loudness -16 LUFS integrated, true peak -1 dBTP across all four films. Captions follow the audio, never lead it.
productionMethod: Playwright renders the exhibit's HTML/SVG/canvas page frame by frame at 1920x1080, 24 fps, driven by one pure function frame(t) per scene (fonts awaited, no CSS transitions), PNG sequence at 2x supersampled then downscaled with Lanczos; subframe accumulation (4 samples at a 180-degree shutter) only for moves above 2 px/frame so motion blur is consistent and photographs are not softened when still. Archive photographs are loaded as raw scans and only scaled and translated, with no color transform; the ground, shadows and graphics sample black point, paper tone and light direction from each plate. Grain: a noise plate is extracted from a flat area of the plate's scan and applied to graphics and ground only, never inside the photograph rectangle. ffmpeg encodes ProRes 422 master then H.264/AAC delivery, with a burned-in-off SRT/WebVTT for captions plus the burned-in version. Lottie/dotLottie for the small recurring ornaments (stamp, lock rules, route dot) so Fabula and Tela can reuse them; the same tokens go into Tela templates and Fabula effect presets so the film matches the exhibit pixel for pixel. Magnific is used only to generate faceless place/object reconstructions or to upscale a failing scan with a before/after check, never for animated video of historical people; any generated frame goes through a human retouch pass and carries the stamp. Pillow handles scan cleaning (dust only, no tonal change), crop-to-mat and contact sheets for review.
risk: The graphics will be so well-integrated that they look like part of the photograph, which is exactly the danger: restraint, labels and the keeping of the plate untouched are the only safeguard, so every graphic that sits near an archive image needs an obvious separation (ground colour change, frame rule) and nothing is ever composited INTO a photograph. Second risk: hand-matching black points per image across 4 films is slow and, done carelessly, becomes a grade by the back door; mitigate with a sampled-value spreadsheet per plate and a rule that any tonal change is on the ground or graphic, never on the plate. Third: four new scripts (Syriac, Chinese, Urdu, Hindi, Punjabi) need native proof and correct shaping in Chromium, or a mistake ships in large type. Fourth: 5000 frames per film at 2x with 4 subframes is heavy; render only moving frames at full cost and cache holds.

arguesWith.why: GENERATIVE will want the paintings animated (Magnific video, painterly morphs between eras, a Ford factory that breathes). Generated motion has no plate: it has its own black point, its own phantom light, a face that drifts between frames, and a floaty camera that was never in a room. It also makes a Reconstruction look like footage, which is a lie of format. I will concede a still reconstruction with a 3 percent honest push and a depth-map parallax of at most 2 percent on faceless place/object scenes, and I will concede generated frames as sources for stills; I will not concede generated video of people, or any morph between a real photograph and a painting.
